ActionTarget.description:
The exact subject a mutation names.

A mutation states the environment, and where it applies the session and epoch, the foreground
application instance and the agent binding revision. Narrower targets leave the fields that do
not apply explicitly null.

agent_binding_revision.description: The agent binding revision, present exactly when `application_instance_id` is.

application_instance_id.description: The foreground application instance, when the effect has one.

environment_id.description: The environment that owns the effect.

session_epoch.description: The session epoch, present exactly when `session_id` is.

session_id.description: The session, when the effect has one.

ActionWindowId.description: A host-issued action window identifier, bound to one authenticated connection and host boot.

ActorEnvelope.description:
The host-constructed identity of one request.

The de-duplication key for a mutation is `(actor_id, action_id)`.

actor_id.description: The stable host-issued principal for this actor.

connection_id.description:
The connection the request arrived on. Closing the control stream revokes every associated
data stream.

controller_generation.description:
The controller generation that admitted the connection. Remote dispatch is fenced when this
generation is replaced.

device_id.description: The paired device, when the ingress is a device.

grant_id.description: The grant the request is being checked against, when one applies.

grant_revision.description: The authority revision the grant was validated at.

ingress.description: Where the request entered the host.

ActorId.description: A stable host-issued principal for one verified actor. The caller cannot assert it.

ActorIngress.description:
Where a request entered the host.

Ingress is part of every authority entry. A method restricted to private IPC is never reachable
through the network or through a plugin component, whatever rights the caller holds.

oneOf.description:
An authenticated operating-system caller on a Unix domain socket or a Windows named pipe.
The host stamps the freshness context; the caller does not pretend to be a paired device.
A paired device on an authorised iroh connection.

A connection that has not passed device authorisation. It reaches only the bounded
pre-authorisation pairing surface.
An automation run acting under an explicit workflow grant on the host.
A plugin component calling a host effect from the plugin runtime.
An installation or host credential presented at a managed or self-hosted service endpoint.

AgentBindingRevision.description: Changes when the active upstream execution owner or selected thread changes.

ApplicationInstanceId.description: One foreground application within a terminal session.

ApprovalRequestId.description: An upstream approval request identifier. Opaque to KalaReach.

AttachmentId.description: One CLI or application attachment, independently of its device.

AuthorityRevision.description: The host's ordered authority revision. Only the host issues its own revisions.

BootEpoch.description: The host boot epoch, which binds continuous-time deadlines to one boot.

BuildId.description: A build identifier reported in hello.

CapabilityId.description: A versioned capability name. Capabilities describe feasibility, never authority.

CapabilityRequirement.description:
Which capability evidence a method requires, and at which revision.

Capabilities describe feasibility. They never create authority.

oneOf.description: No capability evidence beyond the method being listed.

revision.description: The revision the evidence is bound to.

device_key_revision.description: The revision of that device's purpose-separated keys.

offered_versions.description: Every public protocol version the client offers.

ClockEpoch.description: The host clock epoch, advanced when wall-clock trust changes.

ConfirmationRequirement.description: Whether a method needs a fresh owner confirmation.

oneOf.description:
No owner confirmation. Already-authorised restriction, revocation and emergency stop never
need a new rights-enlarging confirmation.

A fresh owner confirmation bound to the exact action digest, destination keys and rights,

A fresh owner confirmation only when the request enlarges persistent authority: a new trust
root, a wider capability ceiling or a persistent grant enlargement.

ConnectionId.description: One transport connection, allocated by the host during hello.

ControllerGeneration.description: The controller's persistent generation, advanced on every controller start.

DeviceKeyRevision.description: The revision of a device's purpose-separated public keys.

DiagnosticId.description: An opaque diagnostic identifier. It carries no protocol meaning.

Digest256.description: A 32-byte SHA-256 digest. On the wire it is a CBOR byte string; in JSON it is unpadded base64url.

DurationMs.description: A duration in milliseconds, as a decimal string in JSON.

EffectClass.description: Whether a method observes state or changes it.

oneOf.description: Observes state. A read never crosses an external-effect boundary and carries no receipt.

EndpointKey.description: A 32-byte iroh endpoint public key. On the wire it is a CBOR byte string; in JSON it is unpadded base64url.

Current authority, expiry and revocation revision are revalidated when the request is

A host-issued action window plus the requested time to live. The host derives the accepted
deadline as the earliest of window expiry, receipt time plus the requested time to live and

The host authority revision it was issued under. The host intersects the grant with current

history.description: How far back it may see.

parent_grant_id.description: The grant this one was delegated from. Revoking a parent revokes its descendants.

recipient_device_id.description: The device it was issued to.

GrantExpiry.description: When a grant stops being valid.

HistoryFilter.description: How the shared host-side history filter applies to a method's result.

oneOf.description: The method returns no retained history or derived content.

The grant's history lower bound applies to every returned event, snapshot, transcript,
attachment reference, export and summary. Derived data identifies its source interval and
is omitted or recomputed when that provenance crosses the viewer's scope.

Live view only: the currently visible screen. Inactive buffers, scrollback and the backing
transcript stay excluded until actually displayed or separately granted.

Current questions or approval resources the grant names explicitly, even when they were
created before the history lower bound. Without that scope the lower bound applies.

HistoryScope.description:
How far back a grant may see, and which current resources it names explicitly.

The lower bound is enforced once, in shared host-side filtering used by event pages, snapshots,
loaded conversations, attachment references, exports, summaries, changed-since-last-visit and
voice context. A later snapshot or a freshly generated summary never makes older underlying
content newly authorised.

include_live_screen.description:
Whether the currently visible screen is included. This exception never grants inactive
screen buffers, scrollback or the backing transcript.

lower_bound_ms.description: The earliest content this grant may see. Null means no retained history at all.

named_approvals.description: Current approval requests named explicitly, on the same terms.

named_questions.description: Current questions named explicitly, even when they were created before the lower bound.

HostSelection.description:
The host's complete `hello` selection.

It echoes the client nonce as well as carrying its own, so the transcript binds one exact

client_nonce.description: The client nonce this selection answers.

device_key_revision.description: The revision of the host's purpose-separated keys.

endpoint_id.description: The host's iroh endpoint identity, validated against the paired record.

IdempotencyBehaviour.description: How a repeated request is resolved.

oneOf.description: An idempotent read. An automatic retry is permitted.

different payload is an `ID_CONFLICT`.

Idempotent under a protocol key. A matching duplicate is acknowledged; a conflicting

key.description: The key the operation is idempotent under.

oneOf.description:
An ordered stream. Positions are acknowledged per connection and never replayed;
reconnecting creates a new stream identity.

MethodName.description: A method name. A name that is not in the registry is denied.

MethodVersion.description:
The version of one method's schema.

Mutation schemas are closed for the negotiated version: an unknown field rejects rather than
being stripped. Read-only metadata may add explicitly optional ignored fields.

MutationRequest.description:
A mutation request.

The payload digest covers the method and version, the actor and grant, the complete target, the
preconditions, the action identifier, the freshness window and time to live, and the
parameters. Replacing the window changes the digest, so it is never an automatic retry.

action_id.description: The durable operation identity, a cryptographically generated UUIDv4.

action_window_id.description: The host-issued action window this first admission is bound to.

expected.description: The subject preconditions this mutation requires.

grant_id.description:
The grant this mutation is claimed under. A local caller's host-stamped context leaves this
null and the host resolves its own owner authority.

request_id.description: Correlates the response. Durable operation identity is `action_id`, not this.

requested_ttl_ms.description:
The requested lifetime. The host derives the accepted deadline and may shorten it. This is
a duration, not permission to refresh a replay.

Nonce256.description: A 32-byte nonce. On the wire it is a CBOR byte string; in JSON it is unpadded base64url.

Notification.description:
One event on a subscribed stream.

Stream sequences are application sequence numbers. Transport streams do not replace them, and a
client that falls behind receives `RESYNC_REQUIRED` rather than holding the read loop.

sequence.description: The position of this event in that stream.

stream_id.description: Which stream the event belongs to.

OrganisationId.description: One organisation whose signed policy a host has opted into.

OrganisationRequirement.description:
An organisation membership requirement attached to a grant.

Organisation leases keep their stricter policy: expired membership blocks further
organisation-mediated reads and mutations even while the transport stays connected.

organisation_id.description: The organisation whose membership the recipient must hold.

policy_revision.description: The policy revision the host has pinned.

oneOf.description: The request succeeded.
The request failed.

ParamsValue.description: An opaque KR-CBOR-1 value. Its shape is defined by the method's own closed schema. The JSON rendering is diagnostic: byte strings appear as unpadded base64url and cannot be told apart from text.

ProtocolError.description:
The error object returned in a response or recorded on a receipt.

The message is plain text for a person or a log. The user interface translates the code into a
direct action and does not display protocol internals by default.

diagnostic_id.description: An opaque identifier for correlating this failure with host diagnostics.

message.description: A plain message. It never carries credentials or command text.

retry.description: How the client may react. It must equal [`ErrorCode::retry_category`] for the code.

major.description: The major version. A mismatch is not negotiable.

minor.description: The minor version. A peer selects the highest minor both sides support.

Receipt.description:
One action receipt.

The de-duplication key is `(actor_id, action_id)`. An exact duplicate returns the stored
receipt; a reused identifier with a different payload digest is an `ID_CONFLICT`.

accepted_deadline_ms.description:
The deadline the host derived at acceptance: the earliest of window expiry, receipt time
plus the requested time to live, and any applicable authority or subject deadline. An exact
retry never receives a new deadline.

actor_id.description: The verified actor that submitted it.

error.description: The failure recorded with a refusal, rejection or unknown outcome.

method.description: The method and version the digest covers.

method_version.description: The method version the digest covers.

payload_digest.description: The digest of the submitted payload, used to detect a reused identifier.

reason.description: Why the action was rejected, when the state is `rejected`.

ReceiptResponse.description:
The response to a mutation request.

A duplicate request from a still-authorised actor returns the retained receipt without
dispatch. The host checks current authority before returning it, so a revoked device cannot use
an old action identifier to retrieve protected information.

request_id.description: The request this response correlates with.

ReceiptState.description: The state of one action receipt.

oneOf.description: The connection acknowledged the request. Transient, never durable acceptance.
The intent is durably committed. No dispatch marker exists yet.
A durable dispatch marker was committed before crossing the external-effect boundary.

The authoritative interface acknowledged the operation. Terminal for admission and
dispatch; later work completion is separate evidence.

The authoritative interface proved the operation was refused without the requested effect.
Terminal. This is not a local pre-dispatch rejection.

Never dispatched. Admission failure, or later expiry, cancellation, revocation or stale
preconditions before dispatch. Terminal.

Dispatch may have occurred. This identifier is never dispatched again. Later authoritative
reconciliation may move it to applied or refused; otherwise it stays unknown.

ReceiveLimits.description:
The receive limits a peer declares.

Both sides state their own bounds; the selection carries the negotiated values and the
transcript covers them, so a downgrade cannot be introduced after `hello`.

max_attachment_frame_len.description: Maximum attachment frame payload, in bytes.

max_control_frame_len.description: Maximum control frame payload, in bytes.

max_input_frame_len.description: Maximum input frame payload, in bytes.

max_send_queue_bytes.description: Maximum queued bytes before the peer is resynchronised.

RejectionReason.description: Why an action was rejected before dispatch.

oneOf.description: Admission failed: authority, preconditions, limits or schema.
The accepted deadline passed before dispatch.
The actor or the host owner cancelled an undispatched intent.
A revocation fenced the action before dispatch.
A subject precondition no longer held in the serial dispatch path.

method.description: The method name. A name that is not in the registry is denied.

method_version.description: The method version. Schemas are closed for the negotiated version.

request_id.description: Correlates the response. Unique for the lifetime of one connection.

RequestId.description: A request identifier, unique for the lifetime of one connection.

RequiredAuthority.description:
What a request must present besides a valid current grant.

An empty required-rights list is not "no check". It means the baseline only: a valid,
unexpired, unrevoked grant for this actor covering the named environment.

oneOf.description: One right from the section 10 action vocabulary.

Ownership of the named resource by the verified actor: its own draft, its own attachment,
its own question or its own undispatched action.
A pairing transcript proof bound to the pinned endpoint identities.
The invitation's issuing-owner context.
A separately created voice grant, intersected with the actor's ordinary grant.
An installation or host service credential presented at a service endpoint.
The registered plugin effect's own declared rights, intersected at dispatch.
The verified originating application or helper and its caller token on private IPC.

RequiredRight.description:
One entry in a method's required-authority list.

A composite action intersects every entry whose condition holds. A configuration or role label
never short-circuits one of these checks.

ResourceSelectorKind.description:
Which resource identities a request names and the host resolves before the authority check.

An attachment's identifier alone is not permission: it selects a resource, and the rights check
still runs against the resolved resource.

RetryCategory.description:
How a client may react to an error.

Only idempotent reads, transfer chunks and requests whose receipt proves no dispatch may retry

oneOf.description:
Do not retry automatically. A new user action, a new subject version or a new action

proves no dispatch may retry, under jittered exponential backoff.
The client's view is stale. Request a new snapshot and resume from the returned cursor.
A configuration or software change is required. Retrying the same request cannot succeed.

Dispatch may have occurred. Never retry this action identifier; show the unknown result and
require a new identifier for an explicit later user request.
